basis: Choanal obstruction, thyroid dysfunction and hearing loss define syndrome; lacrimal anomalies lack evidence of common functional impairment.
Inherited vitamin E deficiency with neurodegeneration; scoliosis/pes cavus and nyctalopia each frequent (30-79%); cardiomyopathy occasional.
Defined as injury to cerebral blood vessels, classified as both cerebrovascular disease and brain injury.
Hepatocellular fibrinogen retention with liver disease and inherited hypofibrinogenemia directly defines both axes.
Peroxisomal bile-acid conjugation enzyme defect; supplied evidence does not establish common hepatic injury or intestinal dysfunction.
Developmental disability, skeletal dysplasia and obesity (4/6) define syndrome; singleton renal and airway findings do not establish common involvement.
Paroxysmal neurologic movement disorder; dystonia and choreoathetosis do not establish primary skeletal muscle damage.
Mitochondrial disorder with neurodevelopmental disease; myopathy supported by ragged-red fibers (2/3) and weakness (2/5); optic atrophy 2/6 and ptosis 3/6.
Definition restricts this benign neoplasm to female reproductive organs; stromal composition does not imply locomotor involvement.
Benign neoplasm arising from cutaneous hair follicles.
Aortic aneurysm and connective-tissue skeletal disease define syndrome; joint hypermobility 8/10 and contractures 4/7; proptosis alone does not establish eye damage.
Progressive autoimmune demyelination of the central nervous system; no additional organ damage meeting the threshold established here.
Congenital adrenal cortical hypoplasia causes primary adrenal insufficiency; neurological grandparent terms do not establish this subtype's phenotype.
Inherited poikiloderma with acral keratoses and hair abnormalities; inflammation alone does not establish an autoimmune mechanism.
Complement regulatory protein deficiency; angioedema is episodic swelling, and associated lupus is a separate disease.
Inherited structural dysplasia of the distal fifth-finger phalanx.
Inherited congenital cardiac malformations and conduction abnormalities.
Hereditary keratoconus causes corneal thinning and ectasia.
Anencephaly is a major congenital brain defect; associated adrenal hypoplasia is frequent (30-79%).
Inherited retinal degeneration with progressive visual loss and nyctalopia in 3/3 patients.
Sterile thrombotic vegetations on endocardium define cardiac and coagulation disease; underlying cancer or autoimmunity is separate.
Melanocytic malignancy arising in rectal mucosa; its origin is gastrointestinal.
Arboviral infection umbrella usually presenting with nonspecific fever; encephalitis and hemorrhage do not characterize most patients across the group.
Immune-complex vasculitis directly damages cutaneous small vessels; arthralgia and myalgia alone do not establish musculoskeletal damage.
Combined immunodeficiency; cellular magnesium signaling defect does not establish systemic deficiency. Lymphomas and respiratory infections are separate diseases.
